decision.note: Priority reflects current attention value, not repository quality.

strengths: Raw/network capability separation is expressed in architecture, compose contracts, tests, and security invariants.
All six observed quality gates passed on the remediated audited commit.
Every observed third-party GitHub Action is pinned to an immutable reviewed commit SHA with a human-readable version comment.
The security-boundary workflow now directly runs policy, pipeline, agent, deployment-contract, egress, and Model Vault boundary tests.
Model Vault catalog pins upstream model revisions and SHA-256 values.
Release-readiness builds distributions and smoke-installs the wheel in a clean environment.
CI/dev reproducibility now uses a reviewed constraints-ci.txt baseline across tests, security gates, benchmarks, and package builds while keeping pyproject runtime ranges library-friendly.
README, Chinese README, threat model, security policy, contributing guide, citation, changelog, roadmap, and safe demo are present.
Unstructured semantic output remains fail-closed and local-only rather than being marketed as anonymous.

findings.title: GitHub repository profile metadata is empty
evidence: GitHub repository metadata returned description=null, homepage=null, topics=[].
docs/repository-profile.md exists, so the intended values are documented but not applied to the repository profile.
findings.recommendation: Apply the documented description, Safe Demo homepage, and discoverability topics in GitHub repository settings.

findings.title: Most GitHub Actions use mutable tag references
evidence: All observed third-party GitHub Actions in .github/workflows are pinned to full immutable commit SHAs.
Version comments are retained beside pins for reviewability.
The remediated main commit passed all six quality gates.
findings.recommendation: Keep Dependabot or equivalent update review active and only advance pins after CI review.

findings.title: The security-boundary workflow does not explicitly run deployment capability-contract tests
evidence: .github/workflows/security.yml now explicitly runs tests/test_policy.py, tests/test_pipeline.py, tests/test_agent_boundary.py, tests/test_deployment_contract.py, tests/test_egress.py, and tests/test_model_vault.py.
The expanded security-boundary gate passed on audited commit b0eeb3b440efe8c69480028667d06952957dd661.
findings.recommendation: Keep capability-boundary tests inside the named security-boundary gate whenever deployment or model setup architecture changes.

findings.title: CI/development dependency resolution is not locked
evidence: constraints-ci.txt now pins the reviewed top-level runtime, development, security-audit, and build toolchain used by CI.

test, security-boundary, security-audit, benchmark-smoke, release-readiness, and release-build workflows consume the constraints strategy while pyproject.toml retains downstream-friendly runtime ranges.
All six push quality gates passed on exact main commit 7657ec0a0b94fe6a8a91639940273fd06412ee8c, including pip-audit after moving pytest to its audited fixed release.
findings.recommendation: Refresh constraints deliberately under the full test/security suite; consider a fully hashed transitive lock later only if the added maintenance cost is justified.

findings.title: Tag release workflow builds artifacts but does not attest or sign them
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml builds distributions and uploads an artifact.
The project documents integrity/provenance concepts, but the tag workflow does not yet attach a keyless attestation/signature or create a provenance-linked release artifact.
findings.recommendation: Before a mature public release, add artifact provenance/attestation and decide whether GitHub Releases/PyPI publication should be automated.

findings.title: Branch protection and repository rules could not be verified
evidence: The connected GitHub App does not expose repository administration/branch-protection state in this audit context.
findings.recommendation: Manually verify required-status-check and protected-main rules before calling the repository release-hardened.

limitations: This audit did not execute a real multi-gigabyte GGUF model locally.
No claim is made that synthetic data or semantic transformations are formally anonymous.
Repository administration settings such as branch protection were not visible through the connected GitHub permissions.
The public Railway demo was assessed as a static safe-demo architecture, not penetration-tested.
recheck_triggers: Any change that permits row-level synthetic network egress.
Any new remote-model or remote-endpoint capability.
Changes to Model Vault download/source verification.
Release workflow changes or a first public package release.
Changes to hardened compose capability boundaries.
A major rewrite of privacy audit thresholds or semantic-release policy.

reasons: The existing Long Gate repository is already public, so changing visibility later would not erase prior disclosure.
Future genuinely new technical mechanisms may warrant patent/ownership review before they are merged into the public tree.
Keep the existing public/background code stable while developing patent-sensitive or organization-specific extensions privately until reviewed.

evidence: README and supporting docs clearly define local-first privacy scope, threat boundaries, and explicit non-claims.
58 tests passed and six quality gates were green; a real multi-gigabyte GGUF execution was not part of this audit.
Raw/network capability separation, fail-closed egress, deployment-contract tests, and Model Vault boundary tests are executable rather than documentation-only.
Observed third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs; curated models pin upstream revisions and SHA-256 values.
CI/dev direct dependencies and security/build tooling are constrained through constraints-ci.txt across the main validation workflows, and exact-main CI passed.
This is a reviewed constraints strategy rather than a fully hashed transitive lock, so reproducibility is strong but not maximal.
Build artifacts and release-readiness checks exist, but release attestation/signing and a mature publication policy are still open.
README, Chinese README, threat model, security policy, contributing guide, citation, changelog, roadmap, safe demo, and model setup guidance are present.
Architecture, tests, workflows, and security documentation are well aligned; the repository remains pre-1.0 with some release/reproducibility debt.
License, contribution/security/citation surfaces exist, but GitHub description/homepage/topics are still empty and branch protection was not verifiable.
